To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variational statement for the large elastic deformation, and also the three statements for the incremental elastic deformation, each involve independent variation of three fields and include the boundary and the discontinuity conditions.

(1) the variational statement for a large deformation at finite strains, with discontinuous fields, involves three independent fields and includes both the boundary conditions and the jump conditions; (2) the same is true for small deformations at finite strain, superimposed on a large deformation at a finite strain; and (3) the same is also true for small deformat ions at small strains, superimposed, on a large deformation.

the variational principles for finite and incremental elastic deformations with discontinuities, which are given in the present paper, are such that the corresponding functional is stationary when all the three fields are varied independently, subject to the constraints imposed by the boundary and the discontinuity conditions, and that the field equations which result from these variational principles are such that they are satisfied by the solution of the problem considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general theory of large elastic deformations, and of the small incremental deformations superim- posed on the large ones.

a variational statement of the field equations of the large deformation theory of finite elasticity, and of the incremental theory of small elastic deformations, superimposed on large, and with the numerical solution by the finite-element method of the corresponding boundary-value problems.
the development of an efficient numerical method for the finite element solution of problems in large elastic deformation theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the finite element formulation of the large finite deformation problem with discontinuous fields can be carried out by using a variational principle involving three independent fields, namely, the displacement, the stress, and the gradient of deformation fields.
the variational method, in conjunction with the finite-element technique, is a very effective tool for the solution of problems involving discontinuities in the fields.

, for a given problem, the variational statement which is best adapted to the particular finite-element formulation to be used is the one which involves the independent variation of the fields that are to be approximated by the piecewise-linear functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the variational statements presented here are such that, when used in conjunction with the finite-element method of solution, the resulting finite element formulation is such that, in the case of finite deformations, the equilibrium of the deformed state is automatically satisfied and that, in the incremental case, the incremental equilibrium of the state considered is also satisfied.

we have given a variational formulation which is capable of describing the equilibrium and incremental behavior of a finite elastic body with discontinuous displacement, stress, and deformation-gradient fields, in the context of finite strains, and that we have given the corresponding finite-element formulation.

we have developed a general theory for large elastic deformatons at finite strains and for small incremental deformations superimposing the large, and we have shown that it is amenable to the finite-element method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by means of the three-field variational principle, we can treat large deformations at finite strain in a unified manner, including the incremental deformations, without the need to resort to the so-called updated Lagrangian formulation.

, in the context of finite deformation problems with discontinuities, it is advantageous to use independent fields, and that this is particularly the case when the fields involved are approximated by piecewise-linear functions.
the variational statements presented here provide the basis for the development of a numerical method which is capable of handling discontinuous fields.
